Field guide / 04—08

Read paint coverage and coat count

Use the selected product's specifications, not one universal litres-per-wall figure.

Vijeron · Updated 9 October 2026

Find coverage on the product label

Look for estimated square metres per litre for your product and surface. A published estimate can differ from actual use. Check whether it assumes one coat, a particular application method, or a prepared surface.

Calculate each coat

Estimated litres = net area × coat count ÷ coverage per litre per coat. If primer and finish paint are different products, estimate them separately. Round a purchase to the pack sizes actually offered by your supplier.

Check the surface and safety

Very porous or rough surfaces and a strongly contrasting old colour may need a different approach. Do not scrape or sand old coatings without checking material hazards; the EPA lead-paint guidance applies to a US context and does not replace local rules.

Worked example

For 34.7 m², two coats and a label value of 10 m²/L/coat, the estimate is 34.7 × 2 ÷ 10 = 6.94 L before rounding to a pack size.

Pitfall to avoid

Do not treat 10 m²/L as a property of all paints. Enter the selected label's value and check its application conditions.
